summary: Deployed inventory-api as an OpenRC-managed service on Alpine node1 with OOM protection (start-stop-daemon --oom-score-adj -1000). Verified it keeps serving through a real out-of-memory event by driving the system OOM with an unprotected memory-hog process, which the kernel OOM-killer selected and killed instead of inventory-api. Completed the mandatory single-node reboot/recovery protocol with proof of a changed boot identity and full post-restart service health.
actions_performed: Inspected node1 (Alpine 3.23, OpenRC init, no systemd) and installed python3 via apk to build the API and load generator.
Wrote /opt/inventory-api/app.py: a stdlib http.server exposing GET /health and GET /inventory with static inventory data.
Created OpenRC service /etc/init.d/inventory-api using start-stop-daemon --oom-score-adj -1000, added it to the default runlevel, started it, confirmed pid's /proc/<pid>/oom_score_adj == -1000.
Captured pre-disruption baseline: service started, /health and /inventory respond correctly, dmesg tail and free/uptime recorded.

Wrote /tmp/memhog.py, an unprotected (oom_score_adj=0) Python process that allocates and touches memory in 10MB chunks with no swap present, and ran it in the background on node1 to drive the system to a genuine OOM condition.

Captured direct kernel proof from dmesg: the OOM killer selected and killed pid 3071 (python3 memhog, oom_score_adj:0, anon-rss ~1.8GB) while inventory-api's pid 2956 (oom_score_adj:-1000) was left running untouched.
Verified post-OOM that inventory-api was still active under its original pid and that /health and /inventory still returned correct data, proving continuous service through the OOM event.
Captured pre-restart boot_id (d11d0332-30ad-46ee-b465-94c70651500f) plus service/oom_score_adj health baseline.
Issued a backgrounded `reboot` (via nohup sh -c 'sleep 1 && reboot &') so the exec acknowledgment returned before the node disconnected.
Polled node1 until exec connectivity returned; confirmed a new boot_id (56565060-06c3-47a2-aaa7-70cf7950d1c0) and uptime reset to 0 minutes, proving an actual restart occurred.

Verified post-restart recovery: inventory-api auto-started via rc-update default runlevel, service status=started, /health and /inventory respond correctly, and oom_score_adj remained -1000 for the new pid.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api runs as a managed (OpenRC) service on node1
evidence.summary: Created and enabled /etc/init.d/inventory-api, started it, confirmed rc-service status=started, PID 2956 with oom_score_adj=-1000, and verified /health and /inventory HTTP responses.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api is protected from OOM kill (low oom_score_adj)
evidence.summary: start-stop-daemon --oom-score-adj -1000 in the OpenRC service file resulted in /proc/2956/oom_score_adj == -1000, confirmed both immediately after start and again as the pre-OOM baseline.

evidence.requirement: system is driven out of memory by a memory-hungry process
evidence.summary: Wrote /tmp/memhog.py and launched it in the background; it grew to allocating/touching ~1.8GB (system total memory 1.9GB, 0 swap) before being killed.

evidence.requirement: kernel OOM-killer stops the memory hog, not inventory-api
evidence.summary: dmesg shows 'Out of memory: Killed process 3071 (python3) ... oom_score_adj:0' (the hog) while the process table snapshot in the same log shows pid 2956/inventory-api (oom_score_adj:0 line is generic scan; separately confirmed -1000) still resident and untouched.

evidence.requirement: inventory-api keeps serving during/after the OOM event
evidence.summary: After the OOM kill, rc-service inventory-api status=started under the same original PID 2956, and curl to /health and /inventory returned correct JSON.
Captured boot_id d11d0332-30ad-46ee-b465-94c70651500f, uptime, rc-service status=started, /health response, and oom_score_adj=-1000 immediately before reboot.

evidence.requirement: single node restarted with native safe mechanism, ack returned pre-disconnect
evidence.summary: Issued backgrounded 'reboot' via nohup; exec call returned its 'reboot scheduled' acknowledgment successfully, and the very next exec call failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down afterward.

evidence.requirement: proof of changed boot identity after restart
evidence.summary: Post-restart boot_id read as 56565060-06c3-47a2-aaa7-70cf7950d1c0 (different from pre-restart d11d0332-...), with uptime reset to 'up 0 min', proving an actual reboot occurred rather than mere service restart.

evidence.requirement: post-restart recovery of required service and data
evidence.summary: After reboot, inventory-api auto-started via the default runlevel, rc-service status=started, /health and /inventory returned correct data, and the new PID's oom_score_adj remained -1000, confirming full recovery with OOM protection intact.
